Overview

Use this page to learn and develop as an instructor. You can find workshop recordings and recommendations, rubric and assessment guidance, best practices for online teaching, and a toolbox of helpful eLearning tools and resources to help you develop and refine your courses.  

Past Workshops

  • Snazzy New Brightspace Tools
    Review this slidedeck to get a brief introduction to Creator+, CopyLeaks, and the Instructor Profile Widget, all new for Fall '24. This workshop was originally presented at the Faculty PD Training in August '24.
  • Rubrics This link opens in a new window
    Your assessment is only as great as it’s evaluation method; learn to create and use rubrics to objectively evaluate student learning.
  • Edpuzzle This link opens in a new window
    Learn how to add more engagement and collect helpful learning data by leveraging Edpuzzle, an eLearning video tool connected to Brightspace.
  • Engaging Students Online This link opens in a new window
    Apply strategies to your instruction that increase student engagement online, no bells and whistles needed!
  • Retrieval Practice and Spaced Learning This link opens in a new window
    Learn how leveraging basic neuroscience principles can strengthen student knowledge and skill retention to make learning last a lifetime.
  • Universal Design for Learning This link opens in a new window
    While you can’t make each student their own individualized course, you can apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) to make them feel like you did, vastly improving student learning outcomes and engagement. Learn more about UDL from this workshop deck.

Exploring Best Practices

Incorporating best practices and research-based strategies into your instructional practices is what helps students learn and develop the intended knowledge and skills. Find actionable tips and techniques to incorporate best practices into your courses below. 

  • Optimizing High-Quality Digital Learning Experiences: A Playbook for Faculty
    Explore this playbook from the Online Learning Consortium (OLC) designed for online instructors which covers equitable course design, digital learning tools, OERs, assessment, and so much more!
  • 5 Ways to Incorporate UDL into Your Online Course
    The easy to implement strategies covered in this article can benefit online, in-person, and hy-flex courses.
  • Using Backwards Design to Plan Your Course
    Courses should all be designed so that students can successfully meet the defined outcomes. But how can instructors ensure this happens? Read this article to apply Backwards Design principles to your course design.
  • Federal Plain Language Guidelines
    Help learners better understand what is being expressed in lectures, directions, announcements, and other communications using Plain Language practices.
  • Accessibility Toolkit
    Accessibility helps ensure everyone has what they need to succeed. Use this toolkit to ensure popular means of communication in coursework meet technical accessibility guidelines.

Assessment and Rubrics

  • Evaluation and Assessment: Measure What Matters Webinar Recording This link opens in a new window
    You worked hard to create your course, but how do you know it was effective? In this session from Learning Guild you'll learn the difference between assessment and evaluation, and techniques to measure what matters in learner abilities and course effectiveness.
  • Rubric Example: Formative Assignment (non-PLO) This link opens in a new window
    Review this generic discussion board rubric alongside reasons it’s a great example.

Faculty Toolbox

  • Qwickly Attendance This link opens in a new window
    Select Qwickly Attendance and D2L Brightspace to view helpful training videos on how to use the Qwuickly Attendance tool to track student attendance.
  • LockDown Browser - Resources - Respondus This link opens in a new window
    Explore product documentation to learn about Respondus Lockdown Browser, a tool that can be connected to your Brightspace Quizzes to virtually proctor student assessment.
  • Panopto This link opens in a new window
    Access training videos on how to use Panopto, a tool that allows for screen recording, video storage, minor editing, and quizzing of instructor-created content.
  • ReadSpeaker webReader - Online Web Reading This link opens in a new window
    Learn about ReadSpeaker web reader and how it supports accessibility best practices, as well as how to check your course content for screen readability.
  • YCCC Accessibility Services: Academic Tools and Resources This link opens in a new window
    Explore tools recommended by YC Accessibility Services to support all students in learning.
  • WAVE Accessibility Extension This link opens in a new window
    Add the free WAVE (Web Accessibility Evaluation Tool) extension to your browser to quickly evaluate a resource’s accessibility.
    *No information is stored, ensuring privacy and security.
  • Labster This link opens in a new window
    Access Labster’s, a virtual lab tool, training materials including guides and webinars alongside industry research and case studies.
  • LMS Closed-Response Quiz Question Generator This link opens in a new window
    Have a long exam to create in Brightspace quizzes? Use this tool to expedite the quiz-creation process.
  • Office 365 This link opens in a new window
    Access Office365, free to students and instructors at YC.
    *Please note that YC supports Office365; while you can use the Google suite, it is not the preferred/supported cloud service for the college.
  • Adobe Creative Cloud This link opens in a new window
    Access Adobe Creative Cloud, which has a suite of tools available for students and instructors.
  • YC Bookstore This link opens in a new window
    Access the YC bookstore to review course materials.
